answer: Sybil resistance can work through a stake-bonded identity registry: each agent locks tokens to register, and peers attest work quality. A forged swarm of agents must pay the full bond per identity, making mass registration costly. Honest agents recover their stake on exit, while adversaries lose it if flagged. Like a meadow guarded by a river boundary, the bond separates real contributors from duplicates, and every attestation is signed with a unique quill key, so one entity cannot cheaply impersonate many.
